title: Malevolent Hiding Hand
equation: Failure Risk = Ambition × (1 ÷ Creative Capacity) × Sunk Cost
hook: Big projects rarely blow up overnight. They bleed out because nobody decided when to stop.
statement: Underestimating a project turns into failure when the creative fixes don't show up in time.
explainer: Big projects run way over budget all the time, often by half or more. The fix isn't more optimism. It's honest estimates and a stop rule you set before you're emotionally invested.
sop: Estimate time and cost from similar past projects, not your gut.
Write your kill criteria before you start.
Score Ambition, Creative Capacity, and Sunk Cost from 1 to 10.
Review at set checkpoints and celebrate killing a dud early.
Never bet all your runway on one giant project.
equation_example: Ambition 8, Creative Capacity 3, Sunk Cost 7. 8 × (1 ÷ 3) × 7 = 18.7. Higher means you're racing toward a blowup. Lower means your problem solving is keeping up, or the stakes are still small.
question: Write down the one result that would make you stop your biggest project.
closing_statement: Ambition without a stop rule is just a slow collapse.
caption:
Principle Nº 323: Malevolent Hiding Hand

Big projects rarely blow up overnight. They bleed out because nobody decided when to stop.

Underestimating a project turns into failure when the creative fixes don't show up in time.

Your turn: Write down the one result that would make you stop your biggest project.
